# Programme Overview

**Certificate in Financial Market and Algorithmic Trading (CFMAT)** — a 52-week, hybrid,
practitioner-led programme that takes learners from how markets work to researching, building,
risk-managing, automating and paper-trading systematic strategies with Python, databases,
statistics, derivatives, machine learning, NLP/RAG and n8n.

## Why this programme exists

Algorithmic trading is a large and growing share of Indian exchange volumes, and SEBI's
retail-algo framework (February 2025) makes brokers answerable for every algo order. At the same
time, SEBI's studies of F&O traders show that the large majority of individuals lose money. The
market needs people who can build strategies that are tested, explainable, risk-controlled and
compliant — and who can tell an edge from a lucky backtest. Most courses teach either finance or
coding, rarely both to a professional standard, and almost none teach research honesty. CFMAT
joins all three.

1. **Markets first.** Instruments, market structure, derivatives, macro, regulation and costs — the things that turn a backtest into real P&L.
2. **Engineering discipline.** Python, SQL, market-data handling, testing, version control, and an event-driven engine whose strategy code runs unchanged in paper trading.
3. **Research honesty.** Look-ahead bias, leakage, overfitting, purged cross-validation, walk-forward testing, the deflated Sharpe ratio, PBO and false-discovery control are core skills, not footnotes.
4. **Modern AI, used carefully.** Machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, NLP, LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation — each with the evidence for and against it.
5. **Risk, monitoring and compliance built in.** Sizing, limits, kill switches, monitoring and the SEBI framework are taught before anything runs live-like.

## Who it is for

- Graduates in engineering, commerce, economics, mathematics, statistics or computer science aiming at quantitative finance.
- Working professionals in BFSI, IT or analytics moving into trading, risk or fintech roles.
- Discretionary traders who want to make their process systematic and testable.
- CA, CFA and FRM candidates or charterholders who want hands-on quant and programming skills.
- Software engineers and data scientists moving into trading systems or financial AI.

No prior programming is required: four weeks of pre-work and an entry assessment make sure
everyone starts Week 1 with working Python and basic statistics. Six [learning routes](10-learning-routes.md)
tell learners from different backgrounds where to go deeper and where they may test out.

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the programme a graduate can:

1. Explain the structure of Indian and global markets, the life of an order, and how equity, debt, currency, commodity and derivative instruments are priced, margined, charged and settled.
2. Read the macro environment (growth, inflation, RBI policy, the yield curve, the rupee) and measure its effect on markets with event studies and regime labels.
3. Write clean, tested Python to acquire, clean, store, validate and analyse market data in pandas, SQL and columnar stores, including real-time data handling.
4. Apply statistics and time-series methods — distributions, HAC inference, multiple-testing control, regression, stationarity, cointegration, the bootstrap — to financial data.
5. Test technical indicators, candlestick and chart patterns, and fundamental factors as hypotheses, with false-discovery control.
6. Price futures and options, use first- and second-order Greeks, and design, backtest and risk-manage F&O strategies.
7. Design, implement and compare trend, momentum, mean-reversion, statistical-arbitrage and factor strategies, and build new ones from rules in the Strategy Creator.
8. Backtest correctly: Indian costs, no look-ahead or survivorship bias, walk-forward validation, the deflated Sharpe ratio and PBO; use parallel processing to research faster without hiding the trial count.
9. Measure and manage risk (VaR, ES, VaR backtests, stress tests, sizing, Kelly, volatility targeting) and build portfolios of assets and of strategies (min-variance, risk parity, HRP).
10. Explain market microstructure and implement execution algorithms (TWAP, VWAP, POV, Almgren–Chriss) with transaction-cost analysis.
11. Build trading infrastructure — OMS, pre-trade RMS, kill switches, broker adapters, monitoring and n8n automation — in line with SEBI's retail-algo framework.
12. Apply ML, DL and RL to trading without leakage, tune gradient boosting with nested walk-forward optimisation, and build advanced strategies (regimes, GARCH, Kalman pairs, meta-labelling, segment optimisation, ensembles).
13. Build NLP and RAG pipelines that turn news and filings into tested signals and cited answers.
14. Present an original, pre-registered, reproducible strategy — backtested, stress-tested and paper-traded for four weeks — to an industry jury.

## Structure at a glance

Six terms over 52 weeks, with three review-and-bootcamp weeks. The full generated table is in the
[curriculum map](02-curriculum-map.md); the week-by-week plan is in the [academic calendar](04-academic-calendar.md).

| Term | Weeks | Modules |
|---|---|---|
| T0 Pre-work | −3 to 0 | M00 Python, statistics and markets primer (self-paced, entry assessment) |
| T1 Foundations | 1–11 | M01 Markets · M02 Macroeconomics · M03 Python · M04 Statistics · M05 Data engineering · **R1** review, exam, Bootcamp 1 |
| T2 Analysis and Derivatives | 12–19 | M06 Technical and patterns · M07 Factors · M08 Derivatives and Greeks · M09 F&O strategies and second-order Greeks |
| T3 Strategy Research | 20–27 | M10 Strategies · M11 Backtesting · M12 Strategy Studio · **R2** review, exam, Bootcamp 2 |
| T4 Risk, Portfolio and Trading Systems | 28–38 | M13 Risk and sizing · M14 Portfolio management · M15 Microstructure · M16 Market data · M17 Platform and compliance · M18 Monitoring and n8n |
| T5 AI for Trading | 39–47 | M19 ML · M20 DL · M21 RL · M22 NLP, LLMs and RAG · M23 Advanced strategies and HPO · **R3** review, exam, Bootcamp 3 · capstone track |
| T6 Capstone and Career | 48–52 | M24 Paper trading, ethics, career studio, Demo Day |

## Format

- **Weekend live classes** (Saturday and Sunday, 3 h each): concepts, worked examples and cases.
- **Weekday lab clinics** (Tuesday and Thursday evenings, 2 h each) with teaching assistants.
- **Office hours** (Wednesday) and a **quiz-and-peer-review** hour (Friday).
- **Three in-person bootcamps** (3 days each, in Weeks 11, 27 and 47) with a trading-floor simulation.
- **Twenty-four hours of 1:1 mentoring** with a practitioner.
- About **6 hours a week of self-study**.

## What makes it worth ₹10,00,000

The full, generated breakdown is in the [fee plan](03-fee-plan.md). In short: 736 guided hours
(≈ ₹1,359 per hour all-inclusive), small cohorts with one TA per 12–13 learners, three bootcamps
with stay and meals, 24 hours of mentoring, licensed NSE data, a static-IP paper-trading server,
GPU hours, a tested codebase and 30+ labs, NISM vouchers, career services and two years of alumni
access.

## Career pathways

Quantitative analyst or junior quant researcher, algorithmic-trading developer, trading-systems
engineer, derivatives or risk analyst, execution analyst, data scientist or AI engineer in
finance, and systematic trader at a proprietary firm. See [admissions and careers](08-admissions-and-careers.md).
The programme offers career support; it **does not guarantee placement, salaries or trading profits**.
